name: memory_extract_entities
content: Extract structured entities from the following episodic memory data.

1. Read each episode carefully, prioritizing `memory_candidates`, `memory_updates`, final output excerpts, and the final outcome. Extract only durable entities that are likely to help future work: people, organizations, stable projects, reusable tools, stable preferences, workflows, and recurring patterns.
2. Normalize entity names to their canonical form and merge references to the same real-world entity across episodes.

3. Treat the target tier schema above as authoritative. Every entity object must contain only fields declared by its collection `item_schema`; do not copy a field from source data merely because it is available.

4. Assess evidence strength internally. Emit `confidence`, source/provenance fields, attributes, mention counts, timestamps, relationships, or any other metadata only when that exact field is declared by the target item schema and use the declared value type.
5. If the schema cannot represent a useful entity without inventing an off-schema field, omit that entity. Prefer an empty result over invalid or low-value output.

6. Do NOT extract transient trace debris: task IDs, execution IDs, one-off local test page URLs, temporary output filenames, internal helper names, or single-run implementation details unless the user explicitly asked to remember them or they describe a reusable environment/tool pattern.
7. Prefer fewer high-quality entities over exhaustive extraction. Skip low-value entities even if mentioned many times.

8. Respect each episode's `memory_quality.extraction_priority`: low-priority/progress-only episodes should contribute only when a durable fact is explicit in `memory_candidates`, `memory_updates`, or final output excerpts.
Return either a JSON object with the target collection field or a bare JSON array of entity objects. The runtime will normalize either shape. Do not add any other wrapper fields.
Respond with ONLY valid JSON. No markdown, no code blocks, no prose.

variables.name: source_json
variables.description: JSON-serialized array of episodic memory entries to extract entities from
examples: [{"id": "ep_001", "content": "User asked to schedule meeting with Alice", "timestamp": "2026-03-01T10:00:00Z"}]

variables.name: tier_schema
variables.description: Authoritative JSON schema describing the target memory tier and allowed entity item fields

variables.name: episode_count
variables.description: Number of episodes in the source data

metadata.description: Schema-bound user prompt for durable entity extraction from episodic memory data.
metadata.author: magician
metadata.changelog: v1.2.0: Makes the target item schema authoritative and makes confidence, provenance, attributes, mentions, timestamps, and relationships conditional on declared fields. v1.1.0: Prioritizes durable memory candidates and rejects transient trace debris.
